answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks through topological cut verifications and multi-agent auditing. Graph evaluation maps peer clusters: sparse edges identify a vulnerable knoll of cloned identities, while dense honest clusters form a secure mesa. To validate actions, an unpredictable consensus pulse samples randomized auditor quorums. Any collusive fraud triggers stake slashing. By scaling minimum audit stake with sub-cluster cut size, attacker coordination cost scales exponentially.
